title: Gerechtigkeitsbrunnen mit Plastik der Justitia (Hans Gieng, 1543)
description: The Gerechtigkeitsbrunnen (Fountain of Justice) in Bern — the first known blindfolded representation of Lady Justice (1543). Hans Gieng's statue holds sword and scales, blindfolded, standing atop vanquished figures representing worldly power (pope, sultan, emperor, magistrate). A foundational image in the history of legal iconography.
citation_abnt: GIENG, Hans. Gerechtigkeitsbrunnen mit Plastik der Justitia. 1543. 1 escultura, fonte. Bern, Gerechtigkeitsgasse. Bildarchiv Foto Marburg. Disponível em: https://www.bildindex.de/document/que20183316.

title: Justitia (marble head from Porta di Capua)
description: Marble head of Justitia from the Porta di Capua, built under Emperor Frederick II. One of the earliest surviving medieval personifications of Justice as a woman — predating the Renaissance tradition. Connected to the Hohenstaufen revival of Roman legal imagery.
citation_abnt: JUSTITIA (cabeça em mármore da Porta di Capua). 1239–1240. 1 escultura em mármore. Museo Provinciale Campano, Capua. Disponível em: https://www.bildindex.de/document/obj08148970.

title: Die Göttin der Gerechtigkeit nach dem heutigen Geschmacke
description: 'The Goddess of Justice according to contemporary taste' — an Enlightenment-era satirical engraving critiquing contemporary justice through its female allegorical form. Shows how the figure of Justice was deployed as a vehicle for political commentary.
citation_abnt: RODE, Bernhard. Die Göttin der Gerechtigkeit nach dem heutigen Geschmacke. Século XVIII. 1 gravura. Kupferstich-Kabinett Dresden. Disponível em: https://www.bildindex.de/document/obj30110594.

title: Justitia an der Rathausuhr (Esslingen)
description: Justitia figure on the town hall clock of Esslingen am Neckar (1589). Justice as a permanent civic presence on a public timepiece — marking the hours under the gaze of the female allegory of law.
citation_abnt: JUSTITIA an der Rathausuhr, Esslingen am Neckar. 1589. 1 escultura. Altes Rathaus, Esslingen. Disponível em: https://www.bildindex.de/document/obj20553978.

title: Barocke Holzdecke: Personifikation der Gerechtigkeit
description: Baroque wooden ceiling in a Lüneburg residential building with allegorical medallions: Personification of Justice. The female justice figure domesticated — appearing not only in courts and public buildings but in private domestic spaces.
citation_abnt: PERSONIFIKATION der Gerechtigkeit (Barocke Holzdecke). 1660–1780. 1 medalhão em teto de madeira. Lüneburg, Große Bäckerstraße 12. Disponível em: https://www.bildindex.de/document/obj20672587.

title: Allegorie: Justitia (Marcantonio Raimondi)
description: Engraving of Justitia by Marcantonio Raimondi, the most important Italian engraver of the High Renaissance (pupil of Raphael's circle). This print disseminated the Italian Renaissance model of female Justice across Europe.
citation_abnt: RAIMONDI, Marcantonio. Allegorie: Justitia. Início do século XVI. 1 gravura. Bibliotheca Hertziana, Roma. Disponível em: https://www.bildindex.de/document/obj08158050.

title: Allegorie der Justitia und eine weitere weibliche Allegorie
description: Italian drawing or print showing Justitia alongside another female allegorical figure. Early 16th-century example of the pairing of Justice with other virtues (Prudence, Temperance, Fortitude) — the four cardinal virtues personified as women.
citation_abnt: ALLEGORIE der Justitia und eine weitere weibliche Allegorie. 1501–1550. 1 desenho/gravura. Museo Civico, Bassano del Grappa. Disponível em: https://www.bildindex.de/document/obj08108743.

title: Justitia (Hameln, Stiftsherrenhaus)
description: Justitia figure on the Stiftsherrenhaus (Canon's House) in Hamelin, c. 1558. A Weser Renaissance example of Justice as architectural ornament on a residential/ecclesiastical building.
citation_abnt: JUSTITIA (Stiftsherrenhaus, Hameln). c. 1558. 1 escultura arquitetônica. Hameln, Osterstraße 8. Disponível em: https://www.bildindex.de/document/obj20608421.

title: Relief: Gerechtigkeit und Eintracht (Bremen Rathaus)
description: Relief of Justice (Gerechtigkeit) and Concord (Eintracht) on the Bremen Old Town Hall (1596–1605). Female Justice paired with female Concord on a civic building — the visual argument that justice produces social harmony.
citation_abnt: RELIEF: Gerechtigkeit und Eintracht. 1596–1605. 1 relevo. Altes Rathaus, Bremen. Disponível em: https://www.bildindex.de/document/obj20459153.

title: Allegorie der Jus Civile (Christian Wenzinger)
description: Allegory of Civil Law (Jus Civile) by Christian Wenzinger, 1752, at a former Benedictine abbey. Distinction between civil and canonical law personified — Justice in her specifically secular legal form within an ecclesiastical setting.
citation_abnt: WENZINGER, Christian. Allegorie der Jus Civile. 1752. 1 escultura. Sankt Peter, Benedictine Abbey. Disponível em: https://www.bildindex.de/document/obj20677105.

title: Kamin mit Justitia (Leipzig, Altes Rathaus)
description: Fireplace with Justitia in the Leipzig Old Town Hall (c. 1610). Justice as a decorative element on a fireplace in the main council chamber — the warming presence of legal authority in the deliberative space.
citation_abnt: KAMIN mit Justitia (Leipzig, Altes Rathaus). c. 1610. 1 decoração de lareira. Altes Rathaus, Leipzig. Disponível em: https://www.bildindex.de/document/obj30143134.

title: Gerechtigkeit (Allegory of Justice) by Lucas Cranach the Elder
description: Painting showing the personification of Justice as a half-length nude female figure against dark background, holding sword and scales. Inscribed 'GERECHTIGKAEIT'. One of the most influential Renaissance depictions — Cranach's eroticized Justice figure set a visual template that persisted for centuries. Northern Renaissance.
citation_abnt: CRANACH, Lucas, o Velho. Gerechtigkeit. 1537. 1 pintura, óleo sobre painel, 72 × 49,6 cm. Coleção particular. Disponível em: https://lucascranach.org/en/PRIVATE_NONE-P457/.

title: Germania
description: Personificação da Alemanha como mulher guerreira (Germania), pintada por Friedrich August von Kaulbach em agosto de 1914, no início da Primeira Guerra Mundial. A figura feminina erguida aparece com coroa imperial de estilo otoniano, espada desembainhada, escudo heráldico e couraça feminina, em fundo noturno com horizonte em chamas. Kaulbach representa a Alemanha em postura defensiva e bélica, simbolizando a nação armada e pronta para o combate. A obra foi encomendada como resposta visual ao clima de mobilização nacional alemã de agosto de 1914, funcionando como propaganda patriótica de alto refinamento artístico.
citation_abnt: KAULBACH, Friedrich August von. Germania. 1914. 1 pintura (óleo sobre tela). Berlim: Deutsches Historisches Museum. Disponível em: https://www.dhm.de/lemo/bestand/objekt/gemaelde-friedrich-august-von-kaulbach-germania-1914. Acesso em: 28 mar. 2026.

title: Germania — Reichspost / Deutsches Reich Definitive Stamp (Paul Eduard Waldraff)
description: Bust of Germania wearing octagonal imperial crown, holding sword and olive branch. Art Nouveau design personally chosen by Kaiser Wilhelm II. Model: actress Anna Führing. Longest-running German definitive series (22 years). NOT used in colonies (replaced by Yacht issue). Overprinted for occupied territories in WWI.

title: Germania "Belgien" Overprint — Military Occupation Stamp (WWI)
description: Germania definitive stamp overprinted with "Belgien" and revalued in Centimes/Francs for use in German-occupied Belgium during WWI. Same image as DE-GERM-1900 but with additional state inscription marking occupation. First series October 1914, second series May 1916.
